findings.what: A path result opens blobUrl(sha, entry.href), and entry.href is '#/files/<encoded path>', so the link is REPO/blob/<sha>/#/files/docs%2F..., which never opens the file.
findings.why: NAV-4: 'Jump to any ... file path from one input'. searchIndex (src/web/app/data/trace.ts:361) gives a path entry the href `#/files/${seg(path)}`. No app route answers that href, and SiteSearch passes it to blobUrl(sha, path) (repo.ts:10) as the file path. Choosing any path match therefore goes to the GitHub repo root at the snapshot SHA with a junk fragment, not to the file. The path jump half of NAV-4 doesn't work.

findings.what: lanesOf drops every activity line whose agent isn't in the kit's AgentName list, so web-tester, web-builder and kit-builder lines vanish from the ui plan's lanes with no notice.
findings.why: AGENT-2 asks for activity.jsonl as per-agent lanes that show the agents working in sequence. DATA-8 says lines are 'never silently dropped', and HONEST-1 applies too. agentOf (shell/agents.ts) returns null for any name outside main/tester/builder/reviewer/security/investigator/git/david, and `if (agent === null) continue;` skips that line. In docs/trace/ui/U4/activity.jsonl most of the 468 lines are web-tester, web-builder or kit-builder, so this node's own activity page would show only main and git. The FilterBar above still counts every record in matchCount/totalCount, so the lane view and the count disagree. The agents fixture uses only build-plan names, so no test catches this. Needs a fixture line with a ui-plan agent, and either a kit AgentName change or a labelled lane for unknown agents.

findings.what: The path search tests check only that a path option is offered. No unit or e2e test checks where a path result goes, so R1 passed every gate.
findings.why: Anti-oracle: the rule, node and SHA tests each check the URL the choice opens, and the path test checks nothing after the offer. nav-4.test.ts 'part of a path finds the path' checks [kind, label] only and leaves out href. A canned href passes both.

findings.what: The test title says 'Enter on it opens the node page', but the test presses ArrowDown and then clicks the option. It never presses Enter, so keyboard selection is unproven.
findings.why: A test asserts the behaviour its title claims (web-testing rule tag; anti-oracle). Keyboard activation of the combobox result is not exercised anywhere in the U4 suite.

findings.what: The rule-page command `git log --reverse <red>^..<green>` says 'Expect red first ... green last', which doesn't hold when a merge lands between red and green.
findings.why: VERIFY-1: the command must re-check the claim without the UI. U4 itself merged origin/ui (eddb436) between its red and green commits. With a merge, red^..green includes the merged branch's commits, and `--reverse` can list older merged commits before red. The printed expectation is then false even though the trail is fine. Related: on the about page (About.tsx:67), the 'Expect red, stub, green or refactor' text leaves out scaffold, a valid TDD trailer.

findings.what: The 'ruling' kind is mapped in KINDS and KIND_WORDS, but the compiler never emits it and no loop event or fixture holds one. The branch is dead, and HITL-1's rulings are silently absent.
findings.why: Code-quality slop list: dead branch. HITL-1 lists rulings among the decisions. The node acceptance narrows the list to pause, steer, sign-off and merge, so this doesn't block. But the page's question ('What did David decide across the nodes') reads as complete while rulings are recorded only in detail text (for example loop.jsonl:38). Either drop the dead kind, or say on the page that rulings aren't extracted.
